chain.label: P&W approved Volvo's coolant-channel drill change as an 'insignificant' process change, assuming .010 in of later boring/honing removes any drilling damage
chain.trigger: The Pratt & Whitney 'Process Approval Record' noted that the request was characterized as an 'insignificant change'... because subsequent material removal (in the boring and honing phases) was accomplished to a depth of at least .010 inch.

chain.label: Drill breakage/breakdown with chip packing and localized loss of coolant while drilling the fan hub tierod hole at Volvo
chain.trigger: some form of drill breakage or drill breakdown, combined with localized loss of coolant and chip packing, occurred during the drilling process

chain.label: Altered microstructure (recrystallized alpha, up to 52 HRC) with ladder cracking .024 in deep in the tierod hole wall, from which a fatigue crack initiated and propagated from the hub's entry into service
chain.trigger: creating the altered microstructure and ladder cracking in the accident hub... the fatigue cracks initiated from the ladder cracking in the tierod hole and began propagating almost immediately after the hub was put into service in 1990

caused_by.evidence: Drill tests have shown that overheated/work hardened microstructure can be created during rough drilling, but not during subsequent boring and honing operations
the total depth of the altered microstructure created by the drill was about .024 inch, more than twice the depth anticipated by the .010-inch limit set by Pratt & Whitney

chain.label: Volvo's postmanufacture BEA and visual inspections accepted the hub; the condition matched no rejectable template despite a 'manufacturing marks' notation
chain.trigger: the accident hub passed BEA and visual inspections at Volvo following the drilling process that created the anomalous microstructure

caused_by.evidence: although the altered microstructure in the accident hub tierod hole was detectable by BEA inspection methods, Volvo did not identify it as rejectable because the appearance of the tierod hole did not match any of the existing inspection templates showing rejectable conditions

chain.label: Delta's October 27, 1995 fluorescent penetrant inspection failed to detect the 1.36-inch detectable crack (deficient cleaning/flash drying, developer coverage, part tracking and manual handling, and/or incomplete inspector search)
chain.trigger: the failure of Delta Air Lines' fluorescent penetrant inspection process to detect a detectable fatigue crack

caused_by.evidence: the crack was large enough to have been detectable during the accident hub's last FPI at Delta

chain.label: In-service inspection program for critical rotating titanium parts lacked redundancy — no second or alternate (eddy current/ultrasonic) inspection required to catch a missed crack
chain.trigger: Contributing to the accident was the lack of sufficient redundancy in the in-service inspection program.

chain.label: Uncontained fracture of the No. 1 engine front compressor fan hub early in the takeoff roll at about 40 knots
chain.trigger: The left engine fan hub fractured early in the takeoff roll when the airplane was at low speed during normal operation.

caused_by.evidence: One of the radial fractures contained a fatigue crack that originated at two locations on the inboard side of a tierod hole

the probable cause of this accident was the fracture of the left engine's front compressor fan hub, which resulted from the failure of Delta Air Lines' fluorescent penetrant inspection process to detect a detectable fatigue crack
an area of altered microstructure that was created during the drilling process by Volvo for Pratt & Whitney and that went undetected at the time of manufacture
manufacturing and in-service inspection processes currently being used do not provide sufficient redundancy to guarantee that... parts... will remain crack-free through the service life of the part

chain.label: Hub and fan blade debris penetrated the left aft fuselage and cabin interior at seat row 37
chain.trigger: Uncontained engine debris from the front compressor front hub (fan hub) of the No. 1 (left) engine penetrated the left aft fuselage.

caused_by.evidence: A total of 16 holes, punctures, or tears were documented on the left fuselage skin.

chain.label: Loss of electrical power when debris severed the right generator differential protection wires, disabling radios, interphone and PA
chain.trigger: the flightcrew heard a 'loud bang,' followed by the loss of cockpit lighting and instrumentation

caused_by.evidence: Of the 154 wires in the bundle, 146 had been severed. Four of the severed wires were channel differential protection wires

chain.label: Fire erupted on the left engine forward cowling, visible for about 20 seconds
chain.trigger: A fire erupted in the area of the left engine cowling following the engine failure.

caused_by.evidence: According to ground witnesses, the fire was visible for approximately 20 seconds.

chain.label: No communication between cockpit and aft cabin: aft flight attendants initiated an evacuation while the captain, unaware of the fire, damage and injuries, ordered no evacuation and delayed engine shutdown
chain.trigger: The interphone system was inoperative at the critical moment when decisions were being made by the aft flight attendants to evacuate and by the captain not to evacuate.

caused_by.evidence: Loss of electrical power rendered the cockpit radios, the cockpit/cabin interphone, and the PA system inoperative

chain.label: Passengers opened the overwing exits and began evacuating while the airplane was still moving and the engines were running
chain.trigger: he opened the overwing exit while the airplane was still moving about 30 miles per hour even though he was not certain that this was the proper action to take

caused_by.evidence: during the takeoff roll he heard a 'pop' and... passengers then began unbuckling their seat belts, running, and screaming for him to open the exit
emergency exits are sometimes opened by passengers before any evacuation order has been given or any decision has been reached

chain.label: Takeoff rejected; captain retarded throttles and braked the airplane to a stop about 1,350 feet down runway 17
chain.trigger: The takeoff was rejected, and the airplane was stopped on the runway.

caused_by.evidence: The captain took control of the airplane and retarded both throttles to idle. He applied manual brakes and brought the airplane to a gradual stop on the runway.

chain.label: Two passengers in row 37 fatally injured and one seriously injured by debris; one passenger seriously injured jumping from the wing during the uncoordinated evacuation
chain.trigger: Two passengers were killed and two others were seriously injured.

caused_by.evidence: The two passengers who were killed sustained massive head injuries. They were seated on the left side of the airplane in the window and aisle seats of row 37, adjacent to the left engine.
The other seriously injured passenger sustained a fractured ankle when she jumped off the front of the left wing during the evacuation.
